note: S434 - BEST-CASE FEASIBILITY analysis for any hypothetical filter from the 400+ indicator bank. This file CORRECTS an incomplete argument I made in step 41 and it is recorded because the correction runs AGAINST my own convenience: it re-opens a route I had declared closed.
why_this_file_exists: MISSION_4's dedicated warning #3 states that before declaring eternal death I must search the 400+ indicator bank at docs/indicators/. In step 41 I argued this was unnecessary because filtering is arithmetically self-defeating - it reduces n, inflating perm_sd, raising the z and EFDR bars while leaving the absolute lift floor untouched. That argument is TRUE but INCOMPLETE, and this analysis shows exactly where it breaks.
method: A filter can only REMOVE trades, never add or improve them. So the theoretical CEILING of any filter is one that removes ONLY losing trades. I computed that ceiling as a function of how many trades are kept, with perm_sd scaled as 1/sqrt(n) per the engine's own dispersion behaviour.

minimum_sufficient_filter.condition: ALL 74 removed trades must be losers

the_correction.what_step41_got_right: Filtering IS self-defeating at DEPTH. The z and EFDR bars genuinely rise as n falls, and a filter removing half the trades must overcome a perm_sd inflated from 0.867 to 1.227.
the_correction.what_step41_got_wrong: I generalised that to ALL filters. But the required lift gain is only +1.96pp, and at shallow depth the lift gain from removing losers grows MUCH faster than the z bar rises. Removing just 4.1% of trades - if they are all losers - lifts WR from 45.77% to 47.73% while perm_sd rises only from 0.8674 to 0.8858, a 2.1% increase. Lift gains 96% while the bar it must clear gains 2%.
the_correction.consequence: The filtering route is NOT arithmetically closed. It is closed only for DEEP filters. A SHALLOW, HIGHLY SELECTIVE filter remains feasible in principle, and MISSION_4 warning #3 therefore still applies in full.
the_correction.honesty_note: This correction re-opens work I had declared finished and delays the mission's conclusion. I record it because an argument that closes a route by overgeneralising is exactly the kind of convenient reasoning the project's eternal-death rule exists to prevent. Declaring death on an incomplete proof would have been a quiet form of the same error as understating n_trials.

what_this_means_practically.required_filter_precision: A filter must achieve at least 4.1% removal with near-100% loser purity. Since the baseline loses 54.2% of trades, a RANDOM 4.1% removal would take about 2.2% losers and 1.9% winners, moving WR by roughly +0.05pp - two orders of magnitude short. The filter must therefore be genuinely INFORMATIVE, not merely restrictive.
what_this_means_practically.realistic_target: In practice no filter is 100% pure. At 70% loser purity, removing 4.1% of trades yields roughly +0.9pp - still short. Reaching +1.96pp at 70% purity requires removing about 9% of trades, and at 60% purity about 14%. Those depths are still shallow enough that the z bar rises by under 8%, so the route stays open across a realistic purity range.
what_this_means_practically.multiplicity_cost: Every additional filter tested raises n_trials and therefore the H5 bar. n_trials is currently 1296 with an expected-max-z of 3.328. Testing 50 additional filter variants would take n_trials to 1346, raising the bar to roughly 3.34 - a negligible 0.4% increase, because expected-max-z grows as sqrt(2*ln(N)). So the multiplicity cost of a DISCIPLINED search of the indicator bank is small, and this is quantified rather than assumed.
